# Compressed quantile covers and conditional smooth exclusion

This audits the parent's strengthening of the radial-variation argument.
The hypotheses are explicit smooth cap derivatives and independently
available signed radial boundary variations at the finitely many anchors.
The strong convex ambient bump construction in
`candidate 23c5cf376b5f9d55` is a sufficient condition.
Smooth strictly convex individual fibers by themselves are not asserted
to provide independent compatible variations.

Let a finite actual positive fiber family over P be a local minimum of
maximum normalized depth beta. Select a local critical continuous-normal
circuit at each restricted fiber maximizer. In group i write

    H_ij={v_ij dot z+u_ij dot x>=b_ij},
    sum_j rho_ij u_ij=0, rho_ij>0, sum_j rho_ij=1,
    A_i=sum_j rho_ij v_ij, h_i=sum_j rho_ij b_ij=A_i dot z_i.

The closed projected halfspaces G_i={A_i dot z>=h_i} cover P, because
each contains its own index. Where G_i holds, the group covers the entire
continuous fiber. Finite-base Helly selects at most h(P) whole groups
covering P. A group from a nondeep fiber, whose cap masses are strictly
below beta M, cannot cover a deepest point. Therefore the selected
deep-origin groups cover every deepest index. Add the original group
of each nondeep fiber; all these extra budgets remain strictly slack
under small deformations.

Keep every ambient normal fixed. The local quantile construction in
`candidate a0fdd477aa859374` supplies thresholds Q_ij(p,tau)
for cap mass tau. Choose the unique nearby common mass tau_i(p) with

    sum_j rho_ij Q_ij(p,tau_i(p))=A_i dot z_i.

This equation keeps the ENTIRE projected halfspace G_i exactly fixed,
not merely the anchor membership. Thus the compressed covering assignment
persists for every nearby body. All adjusted caps in a group have equal
mass. The maximum of tau_i(p)/M(p) over the selected deepest-origin groups
is consequently an upper comparison for the actual depth, after shrinking
the neighborhood so the nondeep roots remain slack. It touches beta at
the original body and has a local minimum there.

For smooth cap derivatives this finite maximum has gradients

    g_i = sum_j theta_ij B_ij-beta M',
    theta_ij=(rho_ij/S_ij)/(sum_l rho_il/S_il).

Strict separation, if zero were outside their convex hull, would give
a signed body direction decreasing every comparison root. Hence there
are p_i>=0, sum p_i=1, with sum p_i g_i=0. No unique-center, sharp-center,
finite representation of actual depth, or universal rainbow assertion
is needed for this one convex balance.

Let Z be the distinct anchor indices. For a fixed z in Z choose its
deepest continuous point x_z and use the normalized radial boundary
variation delta_z supported on that fiber. Every group anchored at z
has its caps through x_z, even if its originally chosen deepest point
was different: each active cap has nonpositive margin at every deepest
point, while the positive weighted margins at the same index sum to
zero. Thus each margin is zero. A critical cap cannot contain a deepest
point strictly, since moving its boundary inward through that point
removes positive mass from its full-dimensional interior fiber.

It follows that g_i(delta_z)=1/2-beta for groups anchored at z, and
g_i(delta_z)>=-beta for all others. If P_z is the sum of the balance
weights of groups anchored at z, then

    0=sum_i p_i g_i(delta_z)>=P_z/2-beta.

Therefore P_z<=2 beta. Summing over distinct anchor indices gives

    beta>=1/(2|Z|)>=1/(2h(P))>=gamma_d/h(P),

since gamma_d<=1/2 for d>=1 (equality for d=1). The argument also works
without repeated anchors by choosing one group per original index.

This excludes strict counterexamples at attained local minima with the
stated smooth cap derivatives AND independent signed radial variations.
It does not extend those variations to flat facets or to compatibility
equalities among arbitrary smooth fibers. In particular it supplies no
regularization step turning the attained compactified polytopal extremum
into one satisfying the hypotheses.
